threats.name: Early Blight
symptoms: Concentric dark brown rings on older leaves (target spots)
Yellowing margins around spots
Stem lesions near soil line
prevention: Maintain 60cm row spacing to facilitate air circulation
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation; use drip irrigation
Mulch base of plants with straw to prevent fungal spore splashback from soil
Apply Trichoderma viride bio-fungicide during vegetative stage
immediateActions: Prune and safely burn or bury heavily infected lower leaves
Disinfect pruning shears between plants with 70% alcohol
Apply Copper Oxychloride 50 WP (2.5g/L) or Mancozeb 75 WP (2g/L) on affected foliage (follow label guidelines)

threats.name: Late Blight
symptoms: Water-soaked dark lesions on leaf tips
White fuzzy fungal growth under leaves during high humidity
Rapid browning and stem collapse
prevention: Ensure field drainage avoids standing water puddles
Plant certified disease-free seeds or resistant hybrid varieties (e.g., Arka Rakshak)
Avoid working in tomato fields when leaves are wet to prevent pathogen spreading
immediateActions: Immediately destroy severely collapsed plants to prevent entire field epidemic
Apply systemic fungicide Metalaxyl-M + Mancozeb (2g/L) strictly according to CIBRC guidelines
Consult local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) officer immediately

threats.name: Whitefly Infestation & Leaf Curl Virus
symptoms: Tiny white flying insects under leaves
Curling, puckering and reduction of leaf size
Sooty mold growth on honeydew secretions
prevention: Install yellow sticky traps (10-12 traps per acre) at canopy height
Grow 2-3 rows of maize or sorghum as border crop barrier
Spray 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) or Neem oil (3ml/L) preventively
immediateActions: Spray Beauveria bassiana or Verticillium lecanii bio-insecticide (5g/L)
Remove and destroy initial virus-infected stunted plants
If infestation crosses Economic Threshold Level (5-10 nymphs/leaf), apply Acetamiprid 20 SP (0.5g/L) with PPE

threats.name: Septoria Leaf Spot
symptoms: Small circular spots with grey centers and dark borders
Tiny black pycnidia specks inside spots
Severe premature defoliation starting bottom-up
prevention: Practice 2-3 year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops
Stake plants to keep leaves off the ground
Destroy volunteer tomato plants and solanaceous weeds
immediateActions: Strip bottom 12 inches of infected foliage
Spray Chlorothalonil 75 WP (2g/L) or Copper Hydroxide (2g/L)

threats.name: Rice Blast
symptoms: Spindle-shaped diamond eye lesions on leaves
Greyish center with brown borders
Neck rot breaking panicles at heading
prevention: Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer application; split into 3-4 doses
Treat seeds with Pseudomonas fluorescens (10g/kg seed)
Ensure regulated water depth and avoid drought stress in nursery
immediateActions: Drain standing water and re-irrigate fresh water
Apply Tricyclazole 75 WP (0.6g/L) or Isoprothiolane 40 EC (1.5ml/L) at first sign of leaf spots

threats.name: Brown Plant Hopper (BPH)
symptoms: Circular patches of drying plants called 'hopper burn'
Brown nymphs crowding at the stem base just above water line
Plant lodging and total grain loss
prevention: Form 'alleyways' (30cm walking path every 2-3 meters) to allow sunlight and aeration
Alternate wetting and drying (AWD) irrigation instead of continuous submergence
Conserve natural predators like spiders and mirid bugs (Cyrtorhinus lividipennis)
immediateActions: Drain water from field for 3-4 days to break insect breeding cycle
Direct spray at the base of plants: Triflumezopyrim 10 SC (0.5ml/L) or Pymetrozine 50 WG (0.6g/L)

threats.name: Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB)
symptoms: Wavy water-soaked stripes along leaf margins turning yellow then bleach white
Milky bacterial ooze beads on young lesions early morning
prevention: Avoid clipping seedling leaf tips during transplantation
Apply balanced fertilizer with recommended Potash (MOP)
Do not allow irrigation water to flow from infected to healthy fields
immediateActions: Spray Copper Oxychloride (2.5g/L) + Streptocycline (0.1g/L) early morning
Withhold nitrogen application until new healthy tillers emerge

threats.name: Pink Bollworm
symptoms: Rosetted flowers (petals twisted together)
Small entry holes in green bolls plugged with excreta
Premature boll dropping and stained lint
prevention: Install Pheromone traps (Gossyplure) @ 5 traps/acre for monitoring
Release Trichogramma bactrae egg parasitoids @ 60,000/acre at squaring
Avoid extending cotton crop beyond 160 days (terminate ratoon crop)
immediateActions: When trap catches cross 8 moths/trap/day for 3 consecutive days, install mass trapping traps (15/acre)
Apply Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC (0.3ml/L) or Spinosad 45 SC (0.4ml/L) targeting early instar larvae

threats.name: Cotton Leaf Curl Virus (CLCuV)
symptoms: Upward and downward curling of leaves
Thickening of leaf veins ('enation' leaf-like outgrowths underneath)
Severe stunting of plant
prevention: Eradicate weed hosts like Abutilon indicum and Parthenium around borders
Plant CLCuV tolerant hybrids
Control vector whitefly populations rigorously
immediateActions: Rogue out and destroy infected plants showing severe enation in early crop stages
Apply Pyriproxyfen 10 EC (2ml/L) to suppress whitefly egg hatching

threats.name: Yellow / Stripe Rust
symptoms: Bright yellow powdery pustules arranged in parallel linear stripes along leaf blades
Yellow dust adhering to farmer clothes when walking through field
prevention: Sow stripe rust resistant varieties recommended for Northern Plains (e.g., HD 2967, PBW 550)
Avoid late sowing in sub-mountainous high humidity zones
Monitor northern boundary fields frequently from December to February
immediateActions: At first appearance of single yellow stripe foci, spray Propiconazole 25 EC (1ml/L) or Tebuconazole 25.9 EC (1ml/L)

threats.name: Aphids (Wheat Aphid)
symptoms: Greenish-black tiny insects sucking sap from ears and flag leaves
Sticky honeydew turning into black sooty mold
prevention: Conserve Coccinellid predator beetles (Ladybird beetles)
Avoid late nitrogen top-dressing which induces lush succulent growth
immediateActions: If population exceeds 10-15 aphids per ear head, spray Thiamethoxam 25 WG (0.3g/L) or Dimethoate 30 EC (1.5ml/L)

threats.name: Potato Late Blight
symptoms: Water-soaked dark purplish lesions on leaves
White mildew ring under leaflets during fog/dew
Rotting foul-smelling tubers in soil
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed tubers from cold storage
High ridging and earthing up to prevent zoospores washing down to tubers
Preventive spray of Mancozeb 75 WP (2.5g/L) before canopy closure
immediateActions: Spray Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (2.5g/L) or Dimethomorph 50% WP (1g/L)
Cut vines/haulms 10 days before harvest to prevent tuber contamination

threats.name: Chilli Thrips & Murda Disease
symptoms: Leaves curl upward like boat shape
Brown necrotic scarring on leaf undersides and fruit stalks
Stunted growth and bud drop
prevention: Install blue sticky traps (10/acre) specifically attractive to thrips
Intercrop with maize or coriander as trap/barrier crops
Foliar application of Neem oil 10000 ppm (2ml/L)
immediateActions: Spray Spinetoram 11.7 SC (1ml/L) or Fipronil 5 SC (2ml/L)
Alternate chemical groups to prevent rapid insecticide resistance

threats.name: Anthracnose / Fruit Rot (Dieback)
symptoms: Circular sunken spots on ripe fruits with black concentric rings
Twigs dry from tip downwards ('dieback') turning straw colored
prevention: Treat seed with Captan or Thiram (3g/kg seed)
Avoid sprinkler irrigation during fruit ripening stage
Collect and destroy fallen infected fruits
immediateActions: Spray Azoxystrobin 23 SC (1ml/L) or Difenoconazole 25 EC (0.5ml/L) at fruit set

threats.name: Fall Armyworm (FAW)
symptoms: Window-pane feeding marks on whorl leaves
Deep irregular holes and sawdust-like frass inside central whorl
Four elevated black spots arranged in a square on the 8th abdominal segment of larva
prevention: Install FAW pheromone traps (5/acre) immediately upon germination
Apply sand and wood ash (9:1 ratio) or neem cake into plant whorls at 15-20 days
Encourage predatory birds by erecting bird perches (10/acre)
immediateActions: Release egg parasitoid Trichogramma pretiosum @ 50,000/acre
Whorl application of Emamectin benzoate 5 SG (0.4g/L) or Spinetoram 11.7 SC (0.5ml/L)

threats.name: Early Shoot Borer
symptoms: 'Dead heart' drying of central spindle in young shoots (1-3 months old)
Rotten dead heart easily pulled out with offensive odor
prevention: Trash mulching up to 10-15 cm thickness in sugarcane rows
Earthing up at 30-45 days after planting
Release egg parasitoid Trichogramma chilonis @ 20,000/acre
immediateActions: Soil drenching/application of Chlorantraniliprole 0.4 GR @ 7.5 kg/acre during early tillering

threats.name: Red Rot
symptoms: Third and fourth leaves wither and turn yellow
Internal pith turns blood red with crosswise white patches
Alcoholic fermentation smell when cane is split
prevention: Select healthy setts from certified nurseries; hot water treatment at 52°C for 30 min
Sett treatment with Carbendazim 50 WP (1g/L)
Adopt crop rotation with paddy or green manure crops
immediateActions: Immediately uproot and burn infected stools; apply lime in the pit
Do not allow runoff water from infected fields into other cane plots

threats.name: Purple Blotch
symptoms: Sunken purplish-brown elliptical lesions with yellow halo on leaves and seed stalks
Foliage falls over and dies prematurely reducing bulb size
prevention: Avoid planting too densely; maintain proper raised beds
Seed treatment with Thiram (2.5g/kg seed)
Avoid overhead irrigation during humid weather
immediateActions: Spray Mancozeb 75 WP (2.5g/L) mixed with sticker (1ml/L) or Tebuconazole 25.9 EC (1ml/L)

threats.name: Tikka Leaf Spot (Early & Late)
symptoms: Early: Reddish-brown spots with prominent bright yellow halos
Late: Carbon black circular spots without halos mainly on lower leaf surface
prevention: Seed treatment with Trichoderma harzianum (4g/kg seed)
Intercrop with Pearl Millet (Bajra) or Pigeon Pea (Arhar) in 4:1 ratio
immediateActions: Foliar spray of Carbendazim 12% + Mancozeb 63% WP (2g/L) or Hexaconazole 5 SC (2ml/L)
